01-parallel-coords-sparkline-table.visual_critic_note: Deliberate Tol bright palette and adaptive alpha rendering lift it above generic, but the 18px sparklines are barely readable, margins are minimal, and the dense 150-line parallel coords offers no visual relief.
01-parallel-coords-sparkline-table.encoding_integrity_note: Parallel coord y-scales and sparkline scales are data-driven via d3.extent/d3.max; sparkline area baseline correctly anchored at zero; minor issues: fixed 20-bin sparklines ignore subset size (Sturges' rule ignored), and population's log-normal distribution on a linear axis compresses most cities visually with no log-scale fallback.
01-parallel-coords-sparkline-table.stress_test_note: Brush 'brush' event calls updateFilter() on every mousemove with no debounce/RAF, triggering both a full canvas redraw and a synchronous DOM teardown/rebuild of all 6 sparkline SVGs (~360 DOM mutations/sec at 60fps).
01-parallel-coords-sparkline-table.cognitive_load_note: Two-view structure (parallel coords + summary table) is well-managed and the 6-color Tol palette stays under the warning threshold, but 150 lines in the parallel coords produce a visually tangled middle section where regional clustering is hard to read at a glance without brushing.

02-linked-scatterplot-matrix.visual_critic_note: Intentional Paul Tol color palette and KDE diagonals show real design thought, but flat typographic hierarchy (no title, all labels same weight), a tightly-tucked legend, and nothing that elevates it above competent baseline keep it from scoring higher.
02-linked-scatterplot-matrix.encoding_integrity_note: Honest encoding throughout: data-driven domains via d3.extent+nice, zero-based KDE area baseline, principled Silverman bandwidth, index-based brush identity (d._i), fixed-radius dots with categorical color only — no radius deception, truncated axes, or dual-axis fabrication; KDE-only diagonal (no histogram) is a minor smoothing-deception risk but bimodality remains visible.
02-linked-scatterplot-matrix.stress_test_note: The brush handler fires full KDE recomputation (O(n×ticks) per diagonal cell) plus opacity updates across all 2400+ circles on every mousemove with no RAF coalescing or throttle; the dispatch `source` parameter is passed but never checked in the listener, leaving a latent infinite-loop risk if the architecture grows.
02-linked-scatterplot-matrix.cognitive_load_note: Clean 3-color palette separates species clearly across all 16 cells, KDE diagonals reinforce distributions without adding new encoding demands, and the SPLOM reads as one conceptual unit rather than 16 independent views.

03-violin-plot-orchestra.visual_critic_note: The entire 6×12 grid of split violins is crammed into roughly the top quarter of the viewport, rendering each individual violin at ~5px wide — the distribution shapes are completely illegible, reducing the data encoding to indistinguishable specks despite a genuinely thoughtful Tol palette and concept.
03-violin-plot-orchestra.encoding_integrity_note: Violin widths correctly use scaleLinear for density (appropriate for 1D density→width, not area), violinScale domain is data-driven from global maxDensity enabling honest cross-cell comparison, KDE bandwidth=2 is near-Silverman optimal for n=30, and the hardcoded yTempScale [0,120]°F is acceptable as a fixed-unit comparison axis; no baseline, lie-factor, or gap-handling violations apply to this chart type.
03-violin-plot-orchestra.stress_test_note: Fully static visualization with no event listeners, transitions, brush, zoom, or touch handlers — none of the five stress-test failure modes are applicable.
03-violin-plot-orchestra.cognitive_load_note: 72-cell grid (6×12) with only 2 colors and a shared axis is a well-managed small-multiples matrix, but each cell renders so small (~70×90px) that individual violin shapes collapse into unreadable bowtie specks — row-level seasonal patterns read, cell-level distribution detail does not.

04-bee-swarm-census.visual_critic_note: Deliberately chosen Tol colorblind-safe palette and thoughtful additions (percentile lines, callout annotations, side box plot) lift it above generic, but three callouts are cramped together at the high-income tail and the chart uses only the top half of its viewport leaving substantial dead space below.
04-bee-swarm-census.encoding_integrity_note: Log scale correctly disclosed, percentiles computed from data via d3.quantile, fixed-radius dots encode no spurious magnitude, companion box plot uses matching log scale — minor deductions for hardcoded domain [12000,600000] instead of data-derived extent and absent key function (acceptable for static chart).
04-bee-swarm-census.stress_test_note: No brush, zoom, transitions, or cross-view dispatch; force sim runs to convergence upfront; tooltip uses unified pointer events — interaction surface is minimal with no robustness violations.
04-bee-swarm-census.cognitive_load_note: 4-color Tol palette and pre-converged swarm keep the single-view layout readable, but all four education categories intermix throughout the dense swarm body so color offers limited insight into distribution differences, and the three callout annotations cluster tightly in the upper-right corner.

05-crossfilter-flight-explorer.visual_critic_note: Clean layout with a slightly intentional blue (#4477AA over default steelblue), but the defining crossfilter feature — gray background bars showing total distribution vs. filtered — is completely invisible in the unfiltered state since foreground bars fully occlude them, and the overall presentation has no typographic hierarchy or design differentiation beyond adequate spacing.
05-crossfilter-flight-explorer.encoding_integrity_note: Zero baselines correct, Y-domain data-driven via d3.max(allBins), crossfilter semantics properly exclude own panel; docked at 6-7 range because X-domains and bin thresholds are hardcoded constants that would break under shift/scale metamorphic transforms on real data.
05-crossfilter-flight-explorer.stress_test_note: Brush fires unthrottled updateAll() on every mousemove re-binning 2000 records across all 3 panels with no RAF/debounce, and 300ms bar transitions lack .interrupt() so rapid brushing causes mid-flight attribute conflicts.
05-crossfilter-flight-explorer.cognitive_load_note: 3 linked histogram panels with a single monochrome palette and clear bg/fg bar layering keeps cognitive load minimal — the crossfilter pattern is textbook and the layout guides the eye without confusion.

06-qq-plot-confidence.visual_critic_note: Intentional Paul Tol colorblind-friendly palette, layered annotation with curved leader line, and inset histogram show deliberate design, but typographic hierarchy is weak (title and axis labels share near-identical visual weight) and the annotation text crowds the inset slightly.
06-qq-plot-confidence.encoding_integrity_note: Data-driven domains via d3.extent, correct standardization, statistically sound confidence bands, zero-baseline inset histogram, no size/area encoding violations, and no dual-axis fabrication; minor deduction for hardcoded n=200 and 20 histogram bins slightly exceeding data-driven recommendations.
06-qq-plot-confidence.stress_test_note: No brush, zoom, or transitions present; only pointer-event tooltips with trivially lightweight pointermove handlers — stress-test criteria are largely inapplicable to this static visualization.
06-qq-plot-confidence.cognitive_load_note: Single-view layout with 2 colors, a confidence band, reference line, inset histogram, and one annotation form a coherent reading path — each element adds information without competing for attention.

07-density-contour-heatmap.visual_critic_note: The RdBu diverging palette on contours reads well and the canvas/SVG hybrid is technically clean, but the muted fill-opacity on both points and contours makes the density encoding feel washed out, and the flat typographic hierarchy (same weight for axis labels, tick labels, and legend) lacks intentional hierarchy.
07-density-contour-heatmap.encoding_integrity_note: Axes and contour color scale are data-driven (d3.extent, d3.max), no radius deception or zero-baseline violations, but the legend uses a fixed [0,1] domain decoupled from the dynamic contour colorScale([maxVal,0]), and the fixed 20px bandwidth ignores zoom-level data density, risking over-smoothing.
07-density-contour-heatmap.stress_test_note: Brush and dblclick each spawn a new d3.timer without stopping any in-flight timer, so rapid interactions cause two timers to simultaneously mutate xScale/yScale domains, producing jumping or corrupt state; all other patterns are clean (brush fires on 'end' only, no cross-view dispatch, canvas batching avoids DOM storm).
07-density-contour-heatmap.cognitive_load_note: Three well-separated clusters with readable contour bands and a clear density legend keep cognitive load low; the diverging RdBu scale is semantically mismatched for a strictly positive density variable but reads intuitively in practice, and animation quality cannot be assessed from a static screenshot.

08-small-multiples-seasonal.visual_critic_note: Intentional sequential blue palette and clean small-multiples layout with linked crosshair interaction show real design thought, but the three overlapping area fills blur into an indistinct blue wash at panel size, undermining year-over-year comparison, and the chart occupies only the top half of the viewport leaving significant dead space below.
08-small-multiples-seasonal.encoding_integrity_note: Zero baseline correct (y0=plotHeight maps to domain 0), shared y-scale enables honest cross-panel comparison, but y-domain is hardcoded [0,60] rather than derived from data, failing the scaling metamorphic test, and no line.defined() guard exists for missing values.
flags: Update Storm (minor): un-throttled pointermove updates 12 crosshairs + tooltip on every mousemove without RAF or debounce
08-small-multiples-seasonal.stress_test_note: No transitions, no brush/zoom, and Pointer Events API used correctly; only risk is the raw pointermove handler firing synchronous DOM mutations across all 12 panels at 60fps without requestAnimationFrame coalescing.
08-small-multiples-seasonal.cognitive_load_note: 12 panels (well under overload threshold), shared axes, restrained 3-hue sequential palette, and consistent y-scale across all cells make cross-month comparison effortless; the panels are slightly small but readable at this viewport.

09-sparkline-dashboard-table.visual_critic_note: Competent multi-encoding dashboard with intentional Tol palette and sector dots, but sparklines are too small to read meaningfully (16px height), volume bars render as gray blobs, and the win/loss strip is indistinct at row height — the data-ink is there but the ink is too small to matter.
09-sparkline-dashboard-table.encoding_integrity_note: Domains are data-driven with correct zero baselines on volume and bullet charts, key function present on row joins, but the sparkline area uses a global shared price domain (hiding per-row trend shape) and lacks line.defined() for missing-value robustness.
09-sparkline-dashboard-table.stress_test_note: No brush/zoom/drag handlers eliminates Update Storm, Stale Scale, and Touch Fight risks, but every sort click fully tears down and rebuilds 175+ DOM nodes (rows.selectAll('td').remove()) with no .interrupt() guard and a dead CSS transition on tbody rows that would cause jitter if D3 transitions were ever added.
09-sparkline-dashboard-table.cognitive_load_note: 25 rows × 4 distinct in-cell chart types (area sparkline, bar sparkbar, win/loss strip, bullet) creates a moderate learning cost, but shared scales across rows, a restrained 5-color sector palette, and consistent column-level encoding keep the table scannable without feeling overwhelming.

10-strip-plot-marginals.visual_critic_note: Deliberate Tol palette, clean marginal panels with functional brush-linked box plots, and good whitespace — held back slightly by the top marginal strip being compressed into a narrow band that makes jitter hard to read and the regression label sitting awkwardly near the data cloud.
10-strip-plot-marginals.encoding_integrity_note: Scatter/strip/box encoding is structurally honest — no zero-baseline violation (scatter doesn't require it), no radius deception, correct Tukey whiskers — but x/y domains are hardcoded magic numbers ([18,72],[140,310]) rather than data-driven d3.extent, and data joins lack key functions, making the chart brittle under data substitution.
10-strip-plot-marginals.stress_test_note: The brush handler fires on every mousemove with no debounce or RAF: it iterates all 250 dots (DOM attr mutations), updates 500 marginal strip attrs, then fully destroys and recreates box plot elements via selectAll('*').remove() on every frame, causing severe jank during active brushing.
10-strip-plot-marginals.cognitive_load_note: Three-view layout (scatter + two marginals) with 3 categories and 250 points reads cleanly — color separation is good and brushing links all panels coherently — but the 40px marginal strips are cramped enough that the overlaid box plots and jittered points blur together, reducing the marginals from readable summaries to decorative density hints.

11-zoomable-treemap.visual_critic_note: Deliberate Tol palette and breadcrumb navigation show design intent, but 11px semi-transparent black labels on colored tiles hurt readability, there is no typographic hierarchy in the header, and zero paddingTop flattens the parent/child distinction to a barely-noticeable opacity difference.
11-zoomable-treemap.encoding_integrity_note: Treemap correctly encodes area proportional to file size via d3.hierarchy().sum(), zoom rescales via data-driven domain updates, and color is categorical — only minor robustness gap is the missing key function in the data join, which would cause element identity issues if data were re-bound.
11-zoomable-treemap.stress_test_note: Click-only zoom with .interrupt() before every transition, pointer events for unified mouse/touch, synchronous scale domain updates before transition creation, and no cross-view dispatch — all five interaction robustness checks pass.
11-zoomable-treemap.cognitive_load_note: 8-color Tol palette stays perceptually distinct, zoom-to-focus interaction prevents needing to process all 389 leaves at once, and breadcrumb maintains navigation context; main unassessable risk is whether the 750ms simultaneous transition of all cells feels like a swarm or a coherent zoom.

12-sunburst-icicle-morph.visual_critic_note: Intentional Tol bright palette with thoughtful depth-based desaturation and excellent ancestor-highlight hover, but the outer ring is dense with 9px rotated labels that are largely unreadable, undermining the data-ink investment.
12-sunburst-icicle-morph.encoding_integrity_note: d3.partition() with hierarchy.sum() gives honest proportional area encoding in both layouts, but the morph uses 64-point path resampling that approximates shapes during transition and the data join lacks key functions (harmless here since no re-renders occur).
12-sunburst-icicle-morph.stress_test_note: Hover interactions (pointerenter/leave setting opacity on all paths) are not gated by the morphing flag, allowing opacity mutations to race against the 1200ms path transition; no brush/zoom means no update-storm, stale-scale, or infinite-loop risk, and unified Pointer Events eliminates mouse-touch fight.
12-sunburst-icicle-morph.cognitive_load_note: 5-color department palette and depth-saturation gradient are well-managed, but the outermost ring (~100 individual member slices) degrades to unreadable slivers that are only accessible via hover, and the simultaneous morph of 100+ paths cannot be assessed for visual chaos from a static screenshot.

13-radial-dendrogram-edge-bundling.visual_critic_note: Clean canvas/SVG hybrid with a restrained single-accent-color hover interaction, but the dense label ring at 10px with parent-prefix names creates an illegible wall of text that undermines an otherwise competent layout.
13-radial-dendrogram-edge-bundling.encoding_integrity_note: Topological chart with no quantitative encoding violations — d3.cluster() correctly distributes nodes, bundling tension is user-controlled and labeled, but data joins lack key functions and layout constants are hardcoded rather than data-driven.
13-radial-dendrogram-edge-bundling.stress_test_note: Slider input calls drawEdges() synchronously without RAF/debounce, and pointerenter performs O(n×m) mass DOM attribute updates on all SVG circles and text elements on every hover; no transitions, no cross-view dispatch, and pointer events correctly unify mouse/touch.
13-radial-dendrogram-edge-bundling.cognitive_load_note: Edge bundling at 0.85 tension manages 80 edges well and hover-fade interaction is well-designed, but 80+ leaf nodes crammed at 10px around the perimeter creates an illegible label ring, and the absence of per-module color coding forces viewers to rely entirely on interaction to find structure.

14-force-directed-clustering.visual_critic_note: Deliberate Paul Tol-inspired palette with well-separated cluster colors, but cluster labels float over node masses and lack halos or background fills, causing readability issues at cluster boundaries.
14-force-directed-clustering.encoding_integrity_note: scaleLinear maps node value to radius (not area), producing a lie factor for size encoding, though the small range (2–6px) and color-as-primary-channel limit the practical deception; domain [1,5] is hardcoded to synthetic data.
14-force-directed-clustering.stress_test_note: SVG DOM mutations (cluster-label join) and quadtree rebuild both execute inside draw() which fires on every simulation tick, causing unnecessary DOM thrashing throughout the layout phase; pointermove is guard-protected and pointer events API is correctly used, and no transitions mean no mid-flight snap risk.
14-force-directed-clustering.cognitive_load_note: 7 well-separated clusters with perceptually distinct colors read clearly at a glance; canvas rendering keeps 400 nodes/600 edges from becoming a hairball, and the hover-highlight interaction manages detail-on-demand without overwhelming the default view.

15-adjacency-matrix-reorder.visual_critic_note: Deliberate TOL palette with clear community encoding, animated reordering, and a companion degree bar chart show real design intent, but the diagonal highlight color (#FEFBE9) nearly vanishes against the white background and the column labels are cramped at 10px rotated text.
15-adjacency-matrix-reorder.stress_test_note: reorder() starts 750ms transitions on 1225 cells without .interrupt(), so rapid button clicks during animation cause conflicting mid-flight transitions; all other interaction paths are clean (pointermove has a cell-change guard, pointer events API avoids mouse-touch fights, no cross-view dispatch).
15-adjacency-matrix-reorder.cognitive_load_note: 35×35 matrix with clear community block structure, restrained 5-color palette, and a coherent side bar chart; cell size (~14px) is small but sufficient for pattern reading, and the reorder transition moves 1,225 elements simultaneously but as one conceptual unit rather than chaotic noise.

16-sankey-energy-flow.visual_critic_note: Deliberate Paul Tol palette with gradient flows and mix-blend-mode shows real design intent, but the loss node labels ('Transmission Loss: 25 unit', 'Distribution Loss: 15 unit') are clipped at the right viewport edge — a concrete layout bug — and flat 11px system-ui typography throughout leaves no visual hierarchy.
16-sankey-energy-flow.stress_test_note: The drag handler calls sankey.update(graph) and redraws all link paths on every mousemove with no requestAnimationFrame coalescing or dirty-flag throttle; all other interaction traps (loop, stale scale, mid-flight, touch/mouse) are absent or cleanly avoided via Pointer Events API.
16-sankey-energy-flow.cognitive_load_note: Five-stage structure and 6-color palette are well-managed, but the dense crossing flows between Transmission/Distribution and the four sector nodes create a tangled mid-section that's hard to trace, and the loss node labels are clipped outside the viewport.

17-chord-diagram-trade.encoding_integrity_note: Chord arc angles and ribbon widths are correctly derived from d3.chord() using raw matrix values — encoding is proportional and data-driven throughout — minor label truncation ('German') visible but no honesty violations.
17-chord-diagram-trade.stress_test_note: No update storm (pointermove only repositions tooltip via CSS), no feedback loops, no stale closures, mid-flight transitions safely interrupted with .interrupt() before each hover transition, and unified Pointer Events API prevents mouse-touch fights.
17-chord-diagram-trade.cognitive_load_note: Dominant USA-China/Canada/Mexico flows read clearly, but 4 perceptually similar warm/pink hues (China, France, S. Korea, Mexico) blur together in the dense ribbon crossing, and the left-side minor countries have arc segments too small to distinguish without hover.

18-collapsible-tree-search.visual_critic_note: Tree renders clearly and the search highlight accent (#EE6677) is a deliberate touch, but the overall palette is monochromatic gray defaults, typography is flat with no hierarchy beyond size, and the tree occupies only the upper-left third of the viewport leaving a large blank void.
18-collapsible-tree-search.encoding_integrity_note: Tree layout uses proper key functions (d => d.id) for object constancy, data-driven SVG dimensions, and no quantitative encodings to distort — circles are fixed-size identifiers, not magnitude encodings, and descendant count badges are computed accurately.
18-collapsible-tree-search.stress_test_note: Search input fires performSearch→update(root) on every keystroke with no debounce or throttle, triggering full tree layout, DOM data joins, and multiple transitions at 60fps typing speed; no brush/zoom means stale-scale, infinite-loop, and touch-fight traps are absent, and unnamed transitions provide implicit interrupt protection for click interactions.
18-collapsible-tree-search.cognitive_load_note: Progressive disclosure via collapse and search-driven expansion keeps working memory load low at any given view; the initial state shows only ~13 visible nodes across 3 levels, node count badges communicate hidden complexity, and the red highlight+fade system during search cleanly isolates matches — the main risk is that the label placement (internal nodes left, leaves right) reverses mid-tree and may cause momentary confusion when nodes toggle state.

19-circle-packing-zoom.visual_critic_note: Deliberate Tol Bright palette and stroke-only internal circles show real design intent, but at root zoom leaf nodes collapse to nearly identical pale gray blobs, making the color encoding invisible where it matters most.
19-circle-packing-zoom.encoding_integrity_note: D3 pack() correctly encodes hierarchy as area-proportional circles (area-correct by algorithm), color is ordinal/categorical (appropriate), no zero-baseline or lie-factor violations applicable; no key functions in join but data is never re-bound so no corruption risk.
19-circle-packing-zoom.stress_test_note: No .interrupt() call before starting new transitions in zoomTo(), so rapid clicks during the 750ms animation create conflicting tweens that fight over node transforms and r attributes; view is also a mutable closure variable that mid-tween clicks read at an intermediate value, risking positional jumps.
19-circle-packing-zoom.cognitive_load_note: 6-color Tol Bright palette, progressive disclosure via zoom, and breadcrumb navigation keep cognitive load low despite 200+ leaf nodes — root view shows clear category structure, and labels are appropriately suppressed until zoomed in.

20-arc-diagram.visual_critic_note: Intentional Tol palette and arc height encoding show design thought, but 30 nodes crammed onto the baseline create heavy label collision and the arcs above ~ch.15 merge into an illegible rainbow tangle at small render size.
20-arc-diagram.encoding_integrity_note: Arc and stroke encodings are structurally honest, but node radius uses scaleLinear instead of scaleSqrt (lie factor on area), and all scale domains are hardcoded magic numbers rather than derived from data.
20-arc-diagram.stress_test_note: The brush handler mutates attributes on all 80 arc paths and 30 nodes on every mousemove without debouncing or requestAnimationFrame coalescing.
20-arc-diagram.cognitive_load_note: 30 nodes and ~80 arcs create heavy overlap in the center at rest, but the hover-highlight and brush-filter interactions substantially decompress cognitive load during exploration, and the 7-color Tol palette stays distinguishable throughout.
